x-e-e3-01.title: Match Ben's reply to the birthday invitation
x-e-e3-01.goal: Check Ben's reply against each line of the invitation, and tell him in English which parts do not match, giving your evidence.
x-e-e3-01.material:
Birthday invitation (written as text only, with no picture):

You are invited to Yuna's birthday party!
Date: Saturday, June 7. Time: 2 p.m. to 4 p.m.
Place: Yuna's house.
Please bring a small gift. No pets, please.

Her friend Ben sent a reply. "I can come to the party on Sunday with my puppy and a book."
x-e-e3-01.thinking.0: Compare each line of the invitation with each piece of the reply
x-e-e3-01.thinking.1: Tell the parts that are fine from the parts that are a problem
x-e-e3-01.prereq.0: Day words such as Saturday and Sunday
x-e-e3-01.prereq.1: The meanings of pet (반려동물) and gift (선물)
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the parts of Ben's reply that do not match the invitation.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.hint.0: Split Ben's reply into pieces: 'who with', 'what', and 'when'. Then match each piece to a line of the invitation.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.hint.1: Find the 'Date' line and the 'No pets' line first.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.r.a: Put the 'No pets, please.' line next to Ben's words and compare them.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.r.b: Read the 'Please bring' line again to see what it asks people to bring. Think about whether the book goes against that line.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.r.c: Compare the day written on the Date line with the day Ben said.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.r.d: Replying that he will come is in the same direction as what the invitation wants.
x-e-e3-01.s.s1.explain: The party is on Saturday and pets are not allowed, but Ben said he will come on Sunday with his puppy. The book can count as a small gift, and saying he will come is not a problem.
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.prompt: Reply to Ben in one or two English sentences. Tell him the two things that do not match.
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.hint.0: First, write one problem in one sentence.
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.hint.1: In the second sentence, write the other problem. Try to use words from the invitation (Saturday, pets, etc.).
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can you say which line of the invitation each of your two problems came from?
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you avoid making the book (a gift) into a problem? (optional)
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you speak to Ben in a way that would not hurt his feelings?
x-e-e3-01.s.s2.modelNote.1: It is short, but it tells both problems.

x-e-e3-02.title: Pick the lines you need from a bakery sign
x-e-e3-02.goal: Separate the lines of the sign that are really needed to answer the question from the lines that are not, then put those lines together to reach a conclusion.
x-e-e3-02.material:
Bakery sign (written as text only, with no picture):

Happy Bakery
Open: Tuesday - Sunday, 8 a.m. - 7 p.m.
Bread: 2 dollars. Cake: 15 dollars.
Free milk with any cake (until 12 p.m.).

Minsu has 20 dollars. He wants to go on Wednesday at 1 p.m., buy one cake, and get the free milk.
x-e-e3-02.thinking.0: Separate the information you need for the question from the information you do not need
x-e-e3-02.thinking.1: Put several lines together to reach a conclusion
x-e-e3-02.thinking.2: Do not miss the time condition
x-e-e3-02.prereq.1: The meanings of dollar (달러) and free (공짜)
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.prompt: To find out whether Minsu 'can buy it and also get the milk free', which lines of the sign do you absolutely need? Choose all that apply.
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.hint.0: Split Minsu's question into three pieces: 'Is it open?', 'Is there enough money?', and 'Is the milk free?'
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.hint.1: Find one line that holds the answer to each piece.
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.r.a: You can only tell whether the shop is open on Wednesday at 1 p.m. by comparing it with this line.
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.r.b: Minsu only wants to buy a cake. Think about whether the information on this line changes the conclusion.
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.r.c: This is the line used to decide whether 20 dollars is enough to buy a cake.
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.r.d: Whether the milk is free has to do with the time. Compare it with the time Minsu goes.
x-e-e3-02.s.s1.explain: You need three lines: whether the shop is open (Open), the price of the cake (Cake), and the time the milk is free (Free milk). The price of bread has nothing to do with Minsu's question.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.prompt: If you put all the lines you need together, what conclusion is right for Minsu?
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.hint.0: Check the open days, the money, and the milk time one by one, and state your conclusion three times.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.hint.1: Compare whether 'until 12 p.m.' is before or after 1 p.m.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.o.a: If you buy a cake, you also get the milk free
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.r.a: You may have missed the time note at the end of the milk line.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.o.b: The shop is closed, so you cannot buy anything
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.r.b: Check again whether the days and hours on the Open line include the time Minsu goes.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.o.c: 20 dollars is not enough, so you cannot buy a cake
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.r.c: Compare the price of the cake with Minsu's money directly.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.o.d: He can buy the cake, but the milk is not free
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.r.d: This is the thinking that puts all three lines together and checks the time condition too.
x-e-e3-02.s.s2.explain: Wednesday is an open day, and 1 p.m. is earlier than 7 p.m., so the shop is open. The cake is 15 dollars, so he can buy it with 20 dollars. But the free milk is only until 12 noon, so he cannot get it at 1 p.m.

x-e-e3-03.title: Find reading time in Mina's Saturday schedule
x-e-e3-03.goal: Come up with different reading start times that meet all the conditions in the schedule, and explain why the other times do not work.
x-e-e3-03.material:
Mina's Saturday schedule (written as text only, with no picture):

10 a.m.: I can start my free time.
12 p.m. - 1 p.m.: Lunch
1 p.m. - 2 p.m.: Dance class
5 p.m.: Dinner. I must finish before dinner.

Mina wants to read a book for 1 hour. She starts on the hour and finishes on the hour.
x-e-e3-03.thinking.0: Make an answer that meets several conditions at the same time
x-e-e3-03.thinking.2: Explain why some cases do not work
x-e-e3-03.prereq.0: Reading a.m./p.m. times (how to change them to 24-hour numbers, like 1 p.m. = 13, is in the hint)
x-e-e3-03.prereq.1: The meanings of before and after
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.prompt: In the schedule, which time periods are not possible for reading? Choose all that apply.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.hint.0: Change the times in the schedule to 24-hour numbers and draw a time strip.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.hint.1: Separate the empty times from the full times.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.r.a: Check the first line of the schedule to see when free time begins.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.r.b: Look for whether there is an activity written in the schedule at that time.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.r.c: Look at the times of the lunch line and the dance line one after the other.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.r.d: Compare it with the dinner time. Also look for whether there is another activity at that time.
x-e-e3-03.s.s1.explain: Free time starts at 10 a.m., and 12 to 14 are full with lunch and dance. There are no activities in the schedule from 15 to 16 and from 16 to 17, and they end before dinner.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.prompt: Make 3 different times (on the hour) when Mina can start reading. Write them as 24-hour numbers. (Example: 3 p.m. = 15)
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.hint.0: 1 p.m. is 13, and 5 p.m. is 17. Change all the times in the schedule to 24-hour numbers.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.hint.1: She reads for 1 hour, so adding 1 to the start time gives the end time.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.hint.2: Lunch and dance come one after the other, so check whether she can start within that time.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.fail.c0: You need to write it on the hour (1, 2, 3...).
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.ok.c1: It is after free time has started.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.fail.c1: Before 10 a.m. it is not free time.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.fail.c2: If she reads for 1 hour, she goes past 5 p.m. (17).
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.ok.c3: It does not overlap with lunch or dance.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.fail.c3: It overlaps with lunch (12 to 13) or dance class (13 to 14).
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.explain: Reading must start after 10 and end by 17. From 12 to 14 is full with lunch and dance. So she can start at 10, 11, 14, 15, or 16.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.because.prompt: In one or two sentences, write why she must not start at 12 or 13, using the schedule as your evidence. You can write in Korean or English.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.because.hint.0: First, find what is in the schedule at 12.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.because.hint.1: Check 13 the same way, and then put them together in one sentence.
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Can you say which line of the schedule your reason came from?
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: Did you explain by comparing with another time she can start (for example, 14)?
x-e-e3-03.s.s2.because.model.1: At 12 there is lunch and at 13 there is dance class, so she cannot read at those times.

x-e-e3-04.title: Guess Jun's feelings from the drawing contest letter
x-e-e3-04.goal: Each time more of the story is revealed, guess Jun's feelings, and change your judgment when a new clue appears.
x-e-e3-04.material: A short story about Jun is revealed in three parts. Each time you read, guess how Jun feels.
x-e-e3-04.thinking.0: Guess feelings using clues as evidence
x-e-e3-04.thinking.1: Change your judgment with a new clue
x-e-e3-04.thinking.2: Write the reason for the change in English
x-e-e3-04.prereq.0: Feeling words such as happy, sad, sorry, and angry
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.prompt: Read one scene at a time and guess how Jun feels. When a new scene appears, you may change your earlier guess.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.hint.0: Use only what Jun says and does in this scene as your evidence.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.hint.1: Put your guess from the earlier scene next to the clues you have now and compare them.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.0.after: Jun won a prize and jumped up, so happiness fits best.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.0.r.a: Think about whether 'jumps up' and 'won first prize' go with sadness.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.0.r.b: His words and actions are clues pointing in the same direction.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Look for any words or actions that would make you think he is angry.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Check whether it fits with 'jumps up'.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.1.after: Speaking quietly and putting the letter in his bag is an action that tries not to show his joy. You can say that his happiness is mixed with feeling sorry.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Look for any words or actions where Jun is angry.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Compare how speaking quietly and putting the letter in his bag is different from the earlier scene.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.1.r.c: This is a guess that explains all the new words and actions.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.1.o.d: The letter is no longer needed
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Did he throw the letter away, or put it in his bag?
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.2.ask: What kind of person might Jun be?
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.2.after: He said let us draw together and that he wants to see Ara's drawing, so you can see that he cares about Ara.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.2.r.a: Look at who the words Jun suggested are for.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.2.o.b: He wants to show off that he won a prize
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.2.r.b: Look for whether Jun's words mention the prize.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Think about whether 'let us draw together' goes with words of avoiding.
x-e-e3-04.s.s1.reflect: In the second scene, because of the new clues 'quietly' and 'put the letter in his bag', your guess changed from 'happiness' to 'happiness + feeling sorry'. The more clues from words and actions pile up, the more accurate your idea of a feeling becomes.
x-e-e3-04.s.s2.prompt: Write Jun's feelings in one or two English sentences, and include one clue from the story.
x-e-e3-04.s.s2.hint.1: Connect it with because to the thing Jun said or did that made you pick that word.
x-e-e3-04.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can you say which words or actions in the story the feeling word in your writing came from?
x-e-e3-04.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you avoid ending with just 'happy'?

x-e-e3-05.title: Show 'worry' without saying it
x-e-e3-05.goal: Write a short text where the reader can guess the feeling only from actions and body clues, without any feeling word.
x-e-e3-05.material: You are going to write a scene where your friend Mina is worried during a test. A text that says the feeling directly and a text that shows it through actions reach the reader in different ways.
x-e-e3-05.thinking.0: Decide which clues show a feeling
x-e-e3-05.thinking.1: Write using only clues, with no feeling word
x-e-e3-05.thinking.2: Predict what the reader will infer
x-e-e3-05.prereq.0: Feeling words such as worried, nervous, and scared
x-e-e3-05.prereq.1: Easy words such as look, hand, and clock
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.prompt: Of the following three texts, which one makes the reader guess that someone is nervous without using the word 'nervous'?
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.hint.0: Tell apart the texts that have a feeling word and the texts that do not.
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.hint.1: Among the remaining texts, find the one that has a body or action clue.
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.r.a: This text tells the feeling directly with a word. Think about whether it is a text where you guess from clues.
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.r.b: This is how actions and changes in the body become clues to a feeling.
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.r.c: It has only a place and objects. Look for whether there is any action that lets you guess the feeling.
x-e-e3-05.s.s1.explain: From the clues of cold hands and looking at the clock again and again, the reader can guess that she is nervous.
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.prompt: Without using the word 'worried', write two or three English sentences showing a worried person. Make it so that a friend who reads it can guess 'she is worried'.
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.hint.0: Imagine how a worried person moves and what she looks at.
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.hint.1: Write one action in one sentence, and then connect two or three of them.
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can a friend who reads your writing guess it without anyone saying the word 'worry'?
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Does each action go with worry?
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.selfAssess.2: Did you think about whether the same clue could be read as a different feeling (joy, boredom)?
x-e-e3-05.s.s2.modelNote.1: It shows the feeling by writing only action clues.

x-e-e3-06.title: Match the field trip notice to Soyun's message
x-e-e3-06.goal: Compare the notice and a friend's message, find the line that contradicts it, and rewrite it in English.
x-e-e3-06.material:
School field trip notice (written as text only, with no picture):

Field Trip
Date: Thursday, April 10. Meet at the school gate at 8:30 a.m.
Bring: lunch, water, and a hat.
Back at school: 3 p.m.

Soyun sent a message to her friend Eunwoo. Look at it below, one line at a time.
x-e-e3-06.thinking.0: Compare the information in the two texts line by line
x-e-e3-06.thinking.1: Tell a contradiction from something simply left out
x-e-e3-06.prereq.1: Words such as Thursday, gate, and lunch
x-e-e3-06.s.s1.prompt: Choose the one line in Soyun's message that does not match the notice.
x-e-e3-06.s.s1.hint.0: Pair up the Date, Meet, Bring, and Back lines of the notice with Soyun's lines, one by one.
x-e-e3-06.s.s1.hint.1: Among the lines that say the same thing, find the one where a number or a day is different.
x-e-e3-06.s.s1.explain: The notice said to meet at 8:30, but Soyun said 9:30 in line 2. Line 1 (Thursday) and line 4 (back at 3) are the same as the notice. Line 3 left out the water, but it does not go against what the notice says.
x-e-e3-06.s.s2.prompt: Instead of Soyun, rewrite line 2 in one English sentence so that it matches the notice.
x-e-e3-06.s.s2.hint.0: Read the Meet line of the notice just as it is.
x-e-e3-06.s.s2.hint.1: Put in the time and place from that line to finish a 'We meet ...' sentence.
x-e-e3-06.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Is the time you corrected the same as the Meet line of the notice?
x-e-e3-06.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you fix only the problem line, without touching the other lines?
x-e-e3-06.s.s2.modelNote.1: A natural answer with an apology added.

x-e-e3-07.title: Guess the reason from Tom's note
x-e-e3-07.goal: Use the clues in the note to guess why Tom did not ride his bike, and judge which explanation has more evidence.
x-e-e3-07.material:
A note Tom left on the kitchen table (written as text only, with no picture):

Mom, I am at the park.
I took my umbrella and my coat.
I did not take my bike.
Back at 5.

Hana says, "It's because Tom's bike is broken," and Jinwoo says, "It's because it is raining outside."
x-e-e3-07.thinking.0: Judge which of the two explanations has more evidence
x-e-e3-07.thinking.1: Use careful words for a guess that is not certain
x-e-e3-07.prereq.1: The meanings of I think, maybe, and probably
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.prompt: Judging from the information in the note, which of the two explanations has more evidence?
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.hint.0: Find one line of the note that supports each explanation.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.hint.1: Tell apart the explanation that has a line to back it up from the explanation that assumes something not in the note.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.o.a: They are the same. You cannot guess the reason at all from the note
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.r.a: Read the note again line by line to see whether there is a line that lets you guess the reason.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.o.b: Jinwoo's explanation has more evidence. It is because he took an umbrella
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.r.b: A clue in the note connects to the explanation. But the idea that the umbrella may be for rain is a guess.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.o.c: The 'broken' explanation has more evidence. The bike is mentioned
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.r.c: The note does not say the bike is broken. It only says he did not take it.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.o.d: It is because Tom likes walking
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.r.d: Look for whether the note says anything like that.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.explain: The umbrella and the coat are clues about the weather, and the note does not say anything about being broken. So Jinwoo's explanation has more evidence, but it is not certain.
x-e-e3-07.s.s1.acc.0: A careful judgment that points out that the reason cannot be settled from the note alone. But since there is the clue of the umbrella, it is hard to say it cannot be guessed at all.
x-e-e3-07.s.s2.prompt: In one or two English sentences, guess why Tom did not ride his bike. Include one clue from the note, and use a word that shows you are not certain (I think, maybe, etc.).
x-e-e3-07.s.s2.hint.0: Find two words about the weather in the note.
x-e-e3-07.s.s2.hint.1: Make a sentence by putting your ideas into the 'I think ... because ...' pattern.
x-e-e3-07.s.s2.selfAssess.0: Can you say which line of the note your reason came from?
x-e-e3-07.s.s2.selfAssess.1: Did you also think about the chance of another reason (for example, the umbrella is for the sun)?
x-e-e3-07.s.s2.modelNote.1: It connected a clue in the second sentence.

x-e-e3-08.title: Two notes with different piano lesson days
x-e-e3-08.goal: Separate the parts that are the same from the parts that clash in two notes, and choose a question that would show which one is right.
x-e-e3-08.material:
Two notes (written as text only, with no picture):

Note 1 (Dad stuck it on the fridge)
Mina, piano lesson is Wednesday at 4 p.m. Take your music book.

Note 2 (a message from Ms. Park at the music academy)
Hello Mina! Your piano lesson is Tuesday at 4 p.m. Please come five minutes early.
x-e-e3-08.thinking.0: Tell matches from contradictions in two texts
x-e-e3-08.thinking.1: Choose a question that finds the missing information
x-e-e3-08.thinking.2: Judge whether a question helps with the decision
x-e-e3-08.prereq.1: The meanings of lesson (수업) and early (일찍)
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.prompt: Choose all the things the two notes say the same.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.hint.0: Put the two notes into a table split into 'what lesson', 'what day', 'what time', and 'what to bring'.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.hint.1: Find the place where different words are written in the same box.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.r.a: Put the days in Note 1 and Note 2 side by side and compare them directly.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.o.b: That it is a piano lesson
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.r.b: Check what lesson both notes talk about.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.r.c: Compare only the time parts of the two notes.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.r.d: Tell whether it is in only one note or in both notes.
x-e-e3-08.s.s1.explain: Both notes are about a piano lesson and say it starts at 4 p.m. The days are different. The thing to bring (music book) and coming early are in only one note, so they are not contradictions.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.prompt: Which question would show whether Wednesday or Tuesday is right?
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.hint.0: Remember again where the two notes clashed.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.hint.1: Check whether the answer to each question settles on either 'Tuesday' or 'Wednesday'.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.r.a: This is a question that asks directly about the part that clashes.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.r.b: Even if you ask what to bring, the lesson day is not settled. Check whether the question solves the contradiction.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.r.c: The time is already the same in both notes. Think about whether the question asks about the part where the contradiction is.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.r.d: The place is not a problem in the two notes.
x-e-e3-08.s.s2.explain: The contradiction came from the day, so only a question that asks directly about the day solves the problem. The time, the thing to bring, and the place are already the same or are not contradictions. It is best to ask Ms. Park, who sets the lesson.

x-e-e3-09.title: Reply differently to an invitation for two people
x-e-e3-09.topic: A short reply that meets the conditions
x-e-e3-09.goal: Write the same content (thanks, why you cannot come, a different time suggestion) in English, changing your tone for a friend and for an adult.
x-e-e3-09.material:
A message from your friend Sam (written as text only, with no picture):
"Can you come to my house on Saturday at 10 a.m.? We can play games."

You have a class at 10 that day, so you cannot go, but you can go at 2 p.m. Put all three of these in your reply.
1) Say thank you for the invitation
2) Say why you cannot go at 10
3) Suggest a different time
x-e-e3-09.thinking.0: Reply with all the conditions in it
x-e-e3-09.thinking.1: Change your tone to fit who receives it
x-e-e3-09.prereq.0: Easy expressions such as Thank you, can't, and Could I ...?
x-e-e3-09.s.s1.prompt: First, write a one- or two-sentence English reply to Sam in a friendly tone. Include all three conditions.
